title: 1988 AHSME Problem 28
statement: An unfair coin has probability \(p\) of coming up heads on a single toss. Let \(w\) be the probability that, in \(5\) independent tosses of this coin, heads come up exactly \(3\) times. If \(w=\frac{144}{625},\) then

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: there is no value of \(p\) for which \(w=\frac{144}{625}\)

solutions.text:
Here \(w(p)=10p^3(1-p)^2.\) At \(p=\frac{2}{5},\) \[ w=10\left(\frac25\right)^3\left(\frac35\right)^2 =\frac{144}{625}. \] Also \(w(\frac{3}{5})=\frac{216}{625}>\frac{144}{625},\) while \(w(1)=0.\) By continuity there is another solution between \(\frac{3}{5}\) and \(1.\) Hence \(p\) is not unique.

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Write \(w\) as a function of \(p\) using the binomial coefficient
Check one simple value, then compare the function at \(p=\frac{3}{5}\) and \(p=1\)
